fields.title: Australia Student Visa (Subclass 500) from India: Fees and Steps
fields.summary: What you need for the Australia Student visa (subclass 500) from India: the fee from AUD 2,500, English scores, the Genuine Student questions, work rules and the Temporary Graduate visa.
fields.seo_title: Australia Student Visa from India: Subclass 500 Fees & Steps

fields.body_md:
## The short answer

- **Visa:** the Student visa (subclass 500) lets you study a full-time course in Australia. You apply online through **ImmiAccount**, the Home Affairs online account.
- **Visa fee:** **from AUD 2,500** (about **₹1,54,500**). The lower fee is for eligible citizens of Pacific Island countries, Timor-Leste and ASEAN countries, and for some English-course students. India is not on those lists.
- **Money to show:** your first-year course fee, **AUD 29,710** for living costs and **AUD 2,000** for travel. Read the full sum in our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/australia/australia-student-visa-proof-of-funds).
- **Where to apply:** from outside Australia. Since **2 October 2026**, most Student visa applications must be lodged outside Australia.
- **Work:** up to **48 hours a fortnight** while your course is in session.
- **Family:** since **2 October 2026**, most applicants can no longer include a partner or children.

Rupee amounts use **₹61.80 per Australian dollar**, the Reserve Bank of Australia rate for 27 November 2026. Rates move every day and your bank will charge its own rate, so treat the rupee figures as a guide.

## When to apply

You can only apply once you have a **Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)**. A CoE is the official record from your university that you are enrolled in a full-time course registered on **CRICOS**, the government list of courses open to overseas students.

Your CoE must be valid when you apply and when Home Affairs decides your visa. Apply with plenty of time before your course starts. Home Affairs advises you not to book travel until your visa is decided.

Australia's academic year starts in **February or March**. Many education providers also offer a mid-year start in **July**. Check your course for its own intake and deadline. More guides are on our [Australia page](/study-abroad/study-in/australia).

## Documents you need

Home Affairs has a **Document Checklist Tool**. Enter your country of passport and your university, and it lists the evidence you must give. Run it again just before you submit, because the list changes. The tool is updated twice a year, on 31 March and 30 September, and sometimes at other times.

Most applicants attach these:

- **Passport:** the pages showing your photo, personal details, and issue and expiry dates. Add your national identity card if you have one, and proof of any change of name.
- **CoE:** one for every course in your application.
- **Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC):** health insurance for international students. You need it for your whole stay, and the visa is refused if you do not give the details. Your cover must start the day you arrive in Australia, not the day your course starts. Your university may arrange it for you. You can read about it on the [government OSHC page](https://www.privatehealth.gov.au/health_insurance/overseas/overseas_student_health_cover.htm).
- **English test result:** only if the checklist asks for it. See the next section.
- **Proof of money:** only if the checklist asks for it. Home Affairs may still ask for it later. If you must attach it and do not, the visa can be refused without a further request.
- **Genuine Student answers and evidence:** see below.
- **Health and character documents:** you might need health exams. You might also pay for health checks, police certificates and biometrics, which Home Affairs lists as extra costs.

## English test scores

Home Affairs gives these minimum overall scores for a course without an English-course or foundation package. They are for tests taken on or after **7 August 2025**.

| Test | Minimum score |
|---|---|
| IELTS Academic | **6.0** |
| PTE Academic | **47** |
| TOEFL iBT | **67** |

Your test result must usually be from the **2 years** before you lodge your application. Tests taken entirely online or at home are not accepted. For TOEFL, you must choose "Taking TOEFL for Australia" when you register. The department lists other tests and some exemptions on the [Student visa page](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500).

## The Genuine Student requirement

Every applicant must show they are a **genuine student**. This means you are a real applicant who intends to study, and that study is the main reason you are applying. The rule applies to applications lodged on or after **23 March 2024**.

The application form asks four questions. Each answer has a limit of **150 words**, and all answers must be in English.

1. Your current circumstances, including ties to family, community, employment and your finances.
2. Why you chose this course and this university, and what you know about studying and living in Australia.
3. How the course will benefit you.
4. Anything else you want to add.

Attach supporting documents to your ImmiAccount. Home Affairs gives more weight to statements backed by evidence, such as academic transcripts, details of your current job, and tax returns or bank statements. It also says that wanting to apply for permanent residence later does not count against you.

## Steps to apply

1. Get your offer and **CoE** from your university.
2. Arrange **OSHC** for your whole stay.
3. Run the **Document Checklist Tool** and collect your documents.
4. Make sure your money meets the rule in our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/australia/australia-student-visa-proof-of-funds).
5. Create or log in to **ImmiAccount**, fill in the form and attach your documents.
6. Pay the visa application charge. Your application is not valid without it.
7. Answer any request from Home Affairs quickly, and check your ImmiAccount for messages.

## How long it takes

Home Affairs does not give a fixed time. It publishes a **visa processing time guide** that shows how long recently decided applications took. Applications from outside Australia are handled in an order set by a Ministerial Direction. For applications lodged on or after **14 November 2025**, that is Direction 115.

Your priority depends on your course type and on whether your university has reached its limit for new overseas students. Home Affairs says your priority does not change whether you get the visa. Read the [processing priorities page](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-processing-times/visa-processing-priorities/student-visa) before you choose a university.

## How long you can stay

The visa usually runs to **2 months** after a course that is **10 months or longer** and ends from January to October. For a course that ends in November or December, it usually runs to **15 March** of the next year. Your OSHC end date also limits the visa, so buy cover for the right period. See the [length of stay page](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500/length-of-stay).

## Work while you study

The visa lets you work up to **48 hours a fortnight** when your course is in session. Students on a master's by research or a doctorate have no limit. Home Affairs says you should not rely on work to pay for your stay.

## After your degree

The **Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485)** lets you stay and work after you finish. For the Post-Higher Education Work stream you must be **35 or younger** when you apply (exceptions apply), have held a Student visa in the last **6 months**, and have a recent degree from a CRICOS course. The stay is usually between **2 and 3 years**, depending on your qualification. The fee is **from AUD 5,750**, plus an Onshore Application Charge that applies to applications from **28 November 2026**, unless you are exempt. See the [Temporary Graduate visa page](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/temporary-graduate-485/post-higher-education-work).

faq_json.q: How much is the Australia student visa fee for Indian students?
faq_json.a: The Student visa (subclass 500) costs from AUD 2,500, about ₹1,54,500 at ₹61.80 per Australian dollar. Lower fees apply only to some citizens, and India is not one of them.

faq_json.q: Do I need IELTS for an Australia student visa?
faq_json.a: Only if the Document Checklist Tool says you must give an English test result. For a course with no English-course package, the minimum overall IELTS Academic score is 6.0, or PTE Academic 47 or TOEFL iBT 67.

faq_json.q: Can I bring my spouse or children on a Student visa?
faq_json.a: Not in most cases. From 2 October 2026, most Student visa applicants can no longer include family members. Check Home Affairs for the exemptions.

faq_json.q: How many hours can I work on a student visa in Australia?
faq_json.a: You can work up to 48 hours a fortnight when your course is in session. Master's by research and doctoral students have no work limit.

faq_json.q: How long does an Australia student visa take to process?
faq_json.a: Home Affairs gives no fixed time. Use its processing time guide, which shows how long recent applications took. Your priority depends on your course type and your university.

faq_json.q: Can I stay and work after my master's in Australia?
faq_json.a: You may be eligible for the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485). You must be 35 or younger, have held a Student visa in the last 6 months and have a recent degree. The stay is usually 2 to 3 years.
